title: See, from on High, a Light Divine
description: See, from on High, a Light Divine in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 215 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Baptism of Jesus”, where the book credits them to the Exeter Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: See, from on high, a light di-vine On Je-sus' head de-scend! And hear the sacred voice from hea-ven That bids us all at-tend.

lines: See, from on high, a light divine
And hear the sacred voice from heaven
His mission thus confirmed from heaven,
And heavenly wisdom showed to man
The path of heavenly peace he showed
That leads to bliss on high;
Where all his faithful followers here
Shall live, no more to die.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
